name: Head
description: Brain and sleep: alertness, reaction time and mood.

name: Eyes
description: Vision. On long missions the eye can change shape and blur near sight (spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome, SANS). Two checks are logged here, the same kinds NASA uses on the ISS: a near-vision test and an Amsler grid.
alert: Eyesight can change on long missions. In a NASA survey of about 300 astronauts, around 60% of those on long flights reported worse near or distance vision, and for some the changes were still there years after landing. The cause is spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome (SANS): a swollen optic nerve, a flattened back of the eye and a far-sighted shift. Astronauts do not go blind, but vision can stay blurred. Run both eye tests regularly and report any change.

name: Ears and balance
description: The inner ear senses balance. In weightlessness it can cause space motion sickness, with dizziness, nausea and unsteadiness. A daily self-rating tracks it.

name: Arms
description: Arm muscles and grip. Muscles that no longer carry weight lose strength without exercise. A handgrip reading tracks upper-body strength.

name: Kidneys
description: Calcium released from bone in weightlessness raises the risk of kidney stones, and drinking enough water helps. Urine colour is a quick hydration check.

name: Legs
description: Leg bones, muscles and daily activity.

name: Whole body
description: Temperature, body mass and general readings.
